## TL;DR

Fixed the motion lifecycle bug behind skeletons that never entered their pulse state. `PageSkeleton` mounts its root only after the shared delay, so the activity-motion hook now watches the element ref and registers it when it appears. Added a positive motion test, kept the reduced-motion assertion, and restored global stubs in the App shell tests. The unrelated settings contrast issue remains outside this task as the review requested.

## Work and rationale

The review found that `useActivityMotion` only inspected its element ref in `onMounted`. The page skeleton starts hidden, so that ref was null at mount and no observer entry was created. Since the delayed skeleton root appears later, it could never receive `page-skeleton--motion-active`. I changed the hook to track the ref: it registers a newly available root, removes the old observer entry if the element changes, and clears its active state when the root disappears. When `IntersectionObserver` is unavailable, the entry is treated as visible, preserving the hook's non-browser/test fallback behavior.

The new test mounts a delayed skeleton with `prefers-reduced-motion` disabled and asserts both the active class and the pulse animation rule. The existing reduced-motion test continues to assert the static state. This makes the motion test fail for the precise null-at-mount bug instead of merely checking that animation is absent. I also added `vi.unstubAllGlobals()` to the tests that stub `fetch`, so the test file no longer leaks that stub into later tests.

The route and view audit recorded for the task is:

| Page / route | Real content layout | Skeleton shape | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Mission Control `/` | One full-width dashboard content block | One dashboard block | Match; no auto-fit card wrap |
| Work `/work` | Board columns | Board columns using work column count and shared breakpoints | Match |
| Client board `/client-board` | Input board columns | Input board columns using input column count | Match |
| Inputs `/inputs` | Input board columns | Input board columns using input column count | Match |
| Stories `/stories` | Story list | One representative row | Match |
| Checks `/checks` | Check plan / recent runs table | Compact table rows | Representative table |
| Releases `/releases` | Release status and distribution cards | One representative card per loading block | Minimal representative card |
| Deployments `/deployments` | Service rows and branch matrix | Service rows plus one matrix column | Match |
| Dev `/dev` | Target cards | Two target cards | Match |
| Secrets `/secrets` | Secrets table | Compact table rows | Match |
| Agents `/agents` | Agent cards | One representative card | Minimal representative card |
| Settings `/settings` | Grouped settings sections | One row per general section | Match |
| Repo `/repo` | Documentation/context list | One representative row | Minimal representative row |

The existing count and breakpoint tests cover those representative shapes and compare board dimensions with their shared constants. No separate loading-shot fixtures were reintroduced: the live task record has an owner-side accepted-scope note that the capture tool interprets a deliberate `aria-busy` loading state as a missing target. The accepted scope is therefore no loading-state screenshots.

## Approaches tried

I traced the active class from `PageSkeleton` through `useActivityMotion` and verified that the root is conditionally rendered only after the delay. Rather than keeping an otherwise empty wrapper mounted solely for the observer, I made the hook respond to the actual element ref. This keeps lifecycle handling in the shared motion utility and supports other callers that may conditionally mount their observed element.

I left the `setting-desc` contrast concern alone. The review identifies it as a pre-existing issue outside the skeleton task and recommends a separate task; changing a shared settings token here would widen scope without improving the loading behavior.

## Challenges and blockers

The app shell's loading-state screenshot approach is intentionally excluded by the accepted-scope note in the live task record. The current shell timing and layout tests still exercise the state in-process. The review also noted that the shell's outer conditional can remove its wrapper before a leave transition completes; this implementation did not restructure the router shell because the immediate review bug was the inactive motion hook, and changing route rendering would carry broader lifecycle risk.

## Key learnings

Motion hooks used with delayed or conditional components must observe ref changes, not assume the element exists at the parent's mount. A test should assert that motion is enabled when the platform permits it as well as disabled under reduced motion. Global test stubs should be restored in the same test that installs them so test order does not affect results.
